01-mirror-match.thesis: The mirror plot delivers immediate identity feedback via cosine score and matched-ion highlighting — strong for chemists, but the verdict competes with the spectrum for attention.
strengths: Matched vs unmatched fragment distinction is visually clear
Cosine score with plain-language verdict supports two-layer reading
Interactive substance dropdowns enable quick what-if comparisons
Harm-reduction footer correctly separates identity from potency
weaknesses: Score block sits below the chart rather than anchoring the layout
Peak m/z labels can crowd on dense spectra without density control
Hardcoded TOKENS colors bypass CSS variable theming
No reduced label mode for mobile or projection use
01-mirror-match.visualization: Score-forward left rail layout in Design Lab widens the mirror plot and elevates the cosine verdict as a persistent hero metric.

02-chromatogram-explorer.thesis: An excellent teaching surface — tap-to-identify peaks with structure and harm notes — but the stacked detail card under the trace underuses horizontal space on desktop.
strengths: Real retention times ground the synthesized trace in dataset medians
Per-peak classify() colors encode substance class at a glance
Plain-language NOTE copy is harm-reduction aligned
SmilesDrawer integration adds chemist-facing depth on selection
weaknesses: Detail panel stacks below chart instead of side-by-side inspector
Peak labels appear without tier control on minor peaks
Trace fill uses fixed TOKENS.info rather than palette-aware accent
Selected peak state requires full redraw
02-chromatogram-explorer.visualization: Sidebar inspector split places the chromatogram left and substance detail right for asymmetric desktop reading.

11-supply-streamgraph.thesis: The streamgraph tells the supply-shift story viscerally, but quarterly axis labels and the legend compete for vertical space without a collapsible stats layer.

Class-color bands map cleanly to substance semantics
Hover tooltips identify bands without requiring legend lookup
weaknesses: Legend always visible though stream colors are self-evident
Quarterly x-axis labels sparse — no quick stats strip
Band colors hardcoded to TOKENS, not theme-swappable
Wiggle offset can confuse first-time readers
11-supply-streamgraph.visualization: Collapsible quarterly stats strip summarizes band totals without stealing focus from the flowing center chart.

liveNoteTemplates.default: Band colors follow {palette} substance mapping on {theme} chrome.

12-cooccurrence-chord.thesis: The chord diagram surfaces supply recipes powerfully; arc labels on the outer ring need hierarchy when 16 substances compete for angular space.
strengths: Directed ribbons show co-manufacture vs co-use patterns
Hover dimming isolates a substance's partners effectively
Top-16 filter keeps the ring readable
Real co-occurrence counts from aggregate data
weaknesses: Arc labels truncate aggressively without density tiers
No focal emphasis ring on hovered arc
Ribbon opacity fixed — hard to distinguish weak vs strong ties at a glance
Inline labels always on regardless of viewport
12-cooccurrence-chord.visualization: Focal arc emphasis ring on hover strengthens hierarchy and guides the eye to the active substance.

Class colors inline in HTML strings bypass CSS variables
No print/screenshot optimization for light palettes
